newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel keeps pressing Palestinian on security.
newsitem.headline: Israel keeps pressing Palestinian on security.

text.p: Israel grudgingly acknowledged PLO help in finding the body of a kidnapped soldier but said Palestinian authorities must still do more to combat Moslem militants before peace talks could restart.

Israeli leaders said gunmen from the Islamic fundamentalist group Hamas abducted and killed Sergeant Sharon Edri, 19, whose body was found in a West Bank village on Thursday seven months after he disappeared outside an army base in central Israel.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has accused Yasser Arafat of giving a "green light" to "terrorists" to attack Israelis, said the Palestinian leader's security forces had helped to crack the case of the missing soldier.

"In the last part of the operation...the Palestinian Authority arrested two members of the squad and through their arrest we were able to determine finally the place where Edri was buried," he said during a visit to the Netherlands.

But the right-wing leader, who has conditioned a return to peace talks with action by the Palestine Liberation Organisation to stop "terrorism", said it had yet to start cooperating fully with Israel on security matters.

"We continue to expect from the Palestinian Authority that it needs to do its utmost to fight terror," Netanyahu said. "Full cooperation along a wide front...in the fight against terror has yet to be implemented."

PLO officials said Palestinian security chiefs refused a request by U.S. Central Intelligence Agency and Israeli security officials at a secret meeting attended by Arafat in Gaza on Tuesday to restore security ties with Israel.

Israeli-Palestinian peace talks were halted after Israel started work on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 and an explosion in a Tel Aviv cafe killed three Israeli women and a Palestinian bomber three days later.

Violence has flared almost daily in the West Bank, where Israeli troops wounded seven Palestinians with rubber bullets on Thursday in the the partitioned town of Hebron. Israeli soldiers and settlers killed three Palestinians in Hebron on Tuesday.
Netanyahu, trying to soften a statement by his defence chief, said Israel had no desire to retake West Bank towns handed over to Palestinian rule.

Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai, replying to soldiers' questions on the Golan Heights, had said Israel would have "no difficulty" in recapturing the eight towns but it did not want to send in troops.

"It is true that we have the capability to return to the towns but we are not interested, as the defence minister rightly said, of going with this option," Netanyahu told reporters in the Netherlands.

In Washington, U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright warned in a speech of an "unpredictable and dangerous" Middle East situation as PLO officials arrived for talks on reviving the peace process.
Albright was to meet top Palestinian negotiators Saeb Erekat and Mahmoud Abbas in follow-up talks to a White House meeting on Monday between Netanyahu and President Bill Clinton.
But it was the discovery of Edri's body in Sourif, the home village of the Tel Aviv cafe bomber, that grabbed headlines in Israel.
The army said the bomber, Mousa Ghneimat, was one of a six-member Hamas squad responsible for kidnapping and killing Edri just minutes after his abduction.
It said the Hamas men had carried out shootings in or near the West Bank since early 1996, killing seven Israelis.
Two members of the squad were in Israeli custody, two were being held by Palestinian forces, one was at large and Ghneimat was dead, it said.
